claude_code.notes: Richest surface (~30 events). Blocks via exit 2 or hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision; rewrite via updatedInput (pre_tool only). Fail mode is not documented anywhere in this project (notes, docstring, evidence, CHANGELOG) for pre_tool or prompt_submit, so the weaker claim (FAIL_OPEN) is recorded rather than a guess in our own favour -- pre_tool and prompt_submit had rested on FAIL_CLOSED with no basis, the strongest claim in the whole vocabulary, and the only one of its kind unsupported here. PreCompact's block=True was similarly unsupported and is now detect-only; the hooks reference at the time this adapter was written suggests PreCompact's exit 2 writes to stderr without blocking anything. Live capture 2026-08-27 found detection broken against current builds: Claude Code now sends prompt_id, which this adapter treated as proof a payload was Devin's, so 38 of 42 real payloads were claimed by Devin instead and a deny rendered in the wrong dialect. Fixed by discriminating on fields observed from Claude Code rather than on a field it was assumed to lack. A second live round (2.1.247, 2026-08-28) settled the RESPONSE contract, which no capture can show: each event was sent one candidate reply shape per trial and the verdict read off the agent's own behaviour. prompt_submit and stop read a TOP-LEVEL {decision: block, reason} and ignore hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision outright -- the shape this adapter emitted at every event, so every prompt_submit and stop deny it ever produced was silently discarded while the dispatcher reported a block. exit 2 is honoured at both too and is deliberately not used: it collapses to 1 under the PowerShell wrapper some vendors apply, and it leaks the hook's command line into the UI. pre_tool keeps permissionDecision, which was not part of that experiment; the observation-only events now get silence.

verified.method: vendor hooks documentation, plus a live capture on Windows: 120 real payloads across four sessions, every one claimed by this adapter and none carrying a vendor event we do not map. `observed` lists the events actually seen fire; the rest of this row still rests on documentation. Extended 2026-08-28 by a live RESPONSE-contract experiment (3.17.8, Windows): two trials of one silent beforeShellExecution hook against `echo hello`, differing only in failClosed -- without it the command ran, with it the command was blocked. That is what established silence as a hook ERROR here rather than a refusal, and it corrected this row's own note, which had generalised the confound into 'an empty response is not an allow'. It also showed the gate firing twice per command (Cursor retries once unsandboxed) and confirmed beforeShellExecution fires when wired -- the earlier captures never saw it because REVERSE_EVENT_MAP wires preToolUse. Extended 2026-09-23 by a live witness on 3.21.18 (Windows; Grok 4.6 agent; one logging probe registered on every event, then two response trials): generic preToolUse fires for the file-writing tool `Write` with tool_input.file_path and the FULL content before the file lands, and a `{permission: deny}` answered there was honoured -- the file was never created and the agent reported the block. An edit to an existing file arrived as the same `Write` carrying the whole new content, so `Write` is the one write tool this version exposes to hooks (Read, Grep and Shell were the others seen). The stop hook, answered once with `{followup_message: ...}`, re-ran the agent with that message as a turn (loop_count 0, then 1 on the follow-up's own stop), which is the mechanism Claude Code's Stop block delivers: the turn ends, the reason comes back, the agent continues. A silent stop hook ended the turn as it would have, so stop fails OPEN. The chat reply itself is NOT a tool call: nothing fired between the last tool and stop.

cursor.notes: Fails OPEN by default; failClosed:true per hook definition makes it fail closed, and agentseam sets it on every gate it installs. `ask` is accepted by the preToolUse schema but not enforced today, so the adapter denies instead of returning a prompt that would behave as a pass; beforeShellExecution and beforeMCPExecution do honour ask. Separate Tab hooks (beforeTabFileRead, afterTabFileEdit) gate inline completions, and workspaceOpen fires outside any session with no canonical event here. Cursor also loads Claude Code-format hooks -- confirmed live (2026-08-27): with both `.cursor/hooks.json` and `.claude/settings.json` carrying the same probe, every event fired twice, once per config. SETTLED live (3.17.8, Windows, 2026-08-28) by a two-trial experiment differing in one key: a beforeShellExecution hook that exited 0 in SILENCE let `echo hello` run without failClosed, and BLOCKED it with failClosed:true. Silence here is a hook ERROR -- not a refusal, not an abstention. That retires the earlier note's flat 'an empty response is not an allow': the 2026-08-27 rejection it rested on was real, but the hook carried failClosed:true, which hook_config() set on every gate with no way to opt out. Its `matcher` also does not mean the same thing at every event: under beforeShellExecution it is a regex over the COMMAND TEXT, not a tool name, so the "Bash" a caller would reasonably pass matches almost nothing and quietly disables the guard -- the one hook field whose wrong value fails silently, since the install still reports success. What preToolUse's matcher matches was not established here, so hook_config writes NO matcher until one is: no matcher gates every call, which over-gates rather than under-gates, and is the conclusion a sibling guardrail reached independently after shipping this format. A hook agentseam wires here must still answer in-dialect, and now for a proven reason -- these gates install fail-closed by DEFAULT, so a silent adapter would refuse every allowed tool call. The same run recorded two facts nothing here had: the gate fires TWICE for one command (sandbox:true, then sandbox:false on Cursor's own retry), so a policy with side effects double-counts and a deny must hold on both passes; and beforeShellExecution DOES fire when it is wired. Across three capture sessions in which shell commands ran, beforeShellExecution never fired while tool_input.command arrived under preToolUse instead. RESOLVED 2026-08-28, and the cause was our own wiring: REVERSE_EVENT_MAP sends pre_tool to preToolUse, so beforeShellExecution was never installed in those captures. A consumer should still gate shell on pre_tool -- it covers every tool and is the only one that can rewrite -- but not because the dedicated event is absent. WITNESSED 2026-09-23 (3.21.18, Windows): the generic preToolUse gate DOES honour deny for a file write -- `Write` arrives with file_path and the full content, a `{permission: deny}` left the file unwritten -- so the write path is gateable here after all, and `Write` is recorded as the write vocabulary. The stop hook honours `{followup_message}`: the message is posted as the next turn and the agent acts on it, so a refusal at stop is delivered the way Claude Code's Stop block is; silence there ends the turn, so stop fails open. afterFileEdit still accepts nothing back, and the chat reply is not a tool call.

junie.notes: Strongest gate here: PreToolUse returns allow/ask/block and carries updatedInput, so block, ask and rewrite are all native. Its event names and field names are Claude Code's by design; project_path is what separates the two payloads. Project-local hooks in <project>/.junie/config.json are IGNORED by default for safety, so a guardrail committed to a repo does not run for a teammate who clones it -- the user file is the only location that takes effect without --config-location. PermissionRequest inverts the usual default: a hook exiting 0 without a blocking decision approves the action and skips the dialog the user would have seen. Deliberately not installable on its own -- it shares canonical pre_tool with PreToolUse, and install('junie', ['pre_tool']) wires only PreToolUse, since bundling the two would hand a consumer an approve-by-default gate they did not ask for. Wire it by hand if wanted. StopFailure is observability-only and fires on LLM/API failures, not tool failures, so it is not tool_failure and is left unmapped. Non-zero exits other than 2 are warnings and execution proceeds, so this fails OPEN.

tabnine.notes: Eleven events, six of which can block -- including AfterTool, which most agents treat as observation only. Event names are Gemini CLI's exactly; the only documented separator is `timestamp` in Tabnine's base schema, which identifies Tabnine but cannot exclude Gemini, so detect() declines these payloads and the agent must be named explicitly. Fails OPEN unusually broadly: any exit code other than 0 or 2 proceeds, AND stdout that is not valid JSON is treated as a systemMessage and the action is ALLOWED -- so a chatty or crashed hook is a permitted action. Rewrite is advertised in the vendor overview but the field carrying it was not in the documentation read here, so no rewrite is claimed.

vscode_copilot.notes: Two products behind one row, and they do not spell events the same way: HOOKS_BY_TARGET gives VS Code agent mode PascalCase names (Claude Code's exactly) and the GitHub Copilot CLI camelCase ones (sessionStart, userPromptSubmitted, agentStop). This adapter claimed camelCase only until 2026-08-28, so it never claimed a real VS Code payload at all -- those went to claude_code alone and were answered in its dialect, which is right at PreToolUse and wrong everywhere else. `timestamp`, which chatHookService merges into every payload, is what separates the two; Tabnine sends it too, so SessionStart -- the one event name Tabnine and VS Code share -- is left ambiguous rather than guessed. `postToolUseFailure`, previously mapped, claimed and installed for, is in neither vendor's name map: it never existed. Four response dialects, because the consumer reads a different shape at each: PreToolUse takes hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision (ask and updatedInput both native, and updatedInput is validated against the tool's schema and silently discarded if it fails), UserPromptSubmit and PostToolUse take a top-level {decision: block, reason}, Stop and SubagentStop take those two fields nested in hookSpecificOutput and drop the block if the reason is missing, and SessionStart/SubagentStart run under ignoreErrors:true where even exit 2 is swallowed. hookEventName is echoed rather than hardcoded: _toHookResult strips hookSpecificOutput outright when the name does not match the event being run. Fails OPEN, not closed as this row claimed for two weeks: exit 2 blocks, but any other non-zero exit is a NonBlockingError that warns the user and lets the call proceed. Also parses Claude settings.json via hookClaudeCompat, and ignores `matcher` -- it is read and thrown away, so there is no tool filtering and the guard must check event.tool itself. Memory writes arrive as the 'memory' tool (create/str_replace/insert), not file edits. Copilot CLI's own camelCase preToolUse (docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-configuration, read 2026-09-27; vendor docs, not yet witnessed live) sends no event name at all -- {sessionId, timestamp, cwd, toolName, toolArgs} -- so it is claimed by toolArgs and answered with a top-level {permissionDecision, permissionDecisionReason}; it has no input rewrite, so a transform there blocks. Live, Windows, 2026-09-28 (Copilot CLI runtime, one observation): a pre_tool hook whose command errored under PowerShell (the entry then had no `powershell` key) made Copilot deny EVERY tool call ("Denied by preToolUse hook ... (hook errored)"). That is not recorded as fail_mode closed: it is a single uncontrolled run of one runtime, the error was a shell parse failure rather than a hook that started and exited with a chosen non-2 code, and it contradicts the VS Code source reading (any non-zero exit other than 2 is a NonBlockingError) that the open claim rests on. Both may be true -- the CLI runtime and VS Code's own engine may differ -- but until a hook that runs and exits 1 is tried on each, `open` stays and a consumer must not rely on either behaviour. Which of the two products a Windows payload came from is not reliably visible in the payload. The camelCase `agentStop` payload names no event, so it is claimed by `stopReason` and parsed as a stop.

grok.notes: PreToolUse is the ONLY blocking event; everywhere else stdout is ignored. No rewrite: the vocabulary is {decision: deny, reason} and nothing more. Fails OPEN -- timeouts, crashes and malformed output are recorded and the call proceeds. Payload fields are camelCase (hookEventName, toolName) while event values stay PascalCase, which is what separates it from Claude Code, Codex and VS Code Copilot. Reads .claude/settings.json and .cursor/hooks.json too. Project hooks need trust (/hooks-trust or --trust) before they run, so a written config is not yet a live one. Grok Build (2026-10-11): this row IS xAI's Grok Build (the grok binary, https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build), not a separate product; its hooks page https://docs.x.ai/build/features/hooks (last updated 2026-07-02) matches this row's contract, xAI names no rename, and grok_build therefore gets no row of its own. The row predates Grok Build 1.0.13 and is stale against the vendor's newer user guide (https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/blob/main/crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/10-hooks.md, read 2026-10-11 against changelog v1.0.50 of 2026-10-06, https://x.ai/changelog/build): hookEventName now carries snake_case values (pre_tool_use) beside a hook_event_name key with the PascalCase name, payloads add timestamp, permissionMode, promptId and toolUseId, tool names are grok's own (run_terminal_command, search_replace), PreToolUse also takes ask, defer and hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput, and UserPromptSubmit, Stop and SubagentStop accept decision: block. Measured 2026-10-11: a payload shaped like the guide's example was claimed by vscode_copilot, not grok. Since value-based detection (D1) it detects as grok and parses to pre_tool: hookEventName being the snake_case twin of hook_event_name is what separates it, and grok's adapter reads the event from hook_event_name, so the {decision: deny, reason} answer this row records reaches a current build's PreToolUse. gemini_cli.notes: Top-level `decision: allow|deny|ask` + `reason` (not nested); rewrite merges via hookSpecificOutput.tool_input; exit 2 also blocks. Write tools are write_file/replace. codex_cli.notes: Claude-family decision shape (hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision) and Claude-family PascalCase event names (verified against hook_config.rs/schema.rs; an earlier version of this note wrongly said camelCase, sourced from the App Server's separate IDE-facing protocol rather than the CLI hook dialect this adapter speaks). Told apart from Claude Code by turn_id: permission_mode and model were also believed exclusive to Codex and turned out not to be -- a real live-captured Claude Code payload carries permission_mode too, and model cannot discriminate either since Cursor's base hook schema also sends it on every event -- so turn_id is the only one of the three still unrefuted by a real payload. Deny is sent as JSON with exit 0: on Windows Codex wraps hooks in powershell -Command, which collapses exit 2 into 1, so an exit-code deny does not survive that platform. That same PowerShell wrapper will not RUN a command line beginning with a quoted path -- it parses as a string expression, not an invocation -- so installs emit Codex's own commandWindows override carrying the `&` call operator (witnessed live 2026-08-28: without it every hook failed with exit 1 and never executed). Three response dialects, one per event group, because every per-event output struct is deny_unknown_fields and rejects the whole response over a foreign key: pre_tool takes hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision, prompt_submit and stop take a top-level {decision: block, reason}, and the observation-only events accept no verdict at all and get silence. A bare allow is silence everywhere -- permissionDecision:allow is rejected unless it carries updatedInput, and a rejected response fails OPEN. ask is likewise unsupported and degrades to a deny with an explanatory reason. Live capture 2026-08-28 (36 payloads) settled the write vocabulary: Codex sends exactly two tool names, Bash and apply_patch, and BOTH carry only tool_input.command -- apply_patch is the file-writing tool and the patch rides in that string, so event.path and event.content are None on a real write and a content policy has to gate on event.command. The file_path/content/new_string/edits vocabulary previously read here was Claude Code's, copied over on an assumption, and no Codex payload has ever carried it. The same capture showed SessionStart carries no turn_id (it is not turn-scoped) and nothing else separates it from Claude Code's, so detect() now declines on it rather than answering in the wrong dialect.

goose.notes: PreToolUse and Stop are the only events that can block; a block from any other event is ignored. The verdict is the flat {decision: block, reason} body, and a bare allow is silence. No rewrite and no ask: a transform or escalate degrades to a block, never to a silent pass. Fail mode is configurable and only at PreToolUse: a failed hook is fail-open by default, and on_failure: block makes it fail closed -- agentseam's install writes on_failure: block on every hook entry it writes (goose reads it at PreToolUse only). Stop stays fail-open whatever on_failure says, and goose caps consecutive Stop blocks (GOOSE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP). stdout is the decision channel, so a handler that prints a log line to stdout reads as no decision. The event name rides under `event`, not hook_event_name, which is what separates goose's payloads from every other adapter's. PreToolUseResult, BeforeReadFile, BeforeShellExecution and AfterShellExecution are observation-only and parse as unknown; AfterFileEdit is wired as file_changed. SubagentStart/SubagentStop are not emitted. Instruction files reach it through AGENTS.md. Evidence wanted (to test or overturn this row): https://github.com/open-coder-ai/agentseam/issues/177

cline.notes: Adapted (D2b): Cline runs one executable per event from .clinerules/hooks/, named exactly after the event, and reads {"cancel": true, "errorMessage"} on stdout as a block. agentseam speaks that cancel object (grammar G7) at PreToolUse only, the one event whose cancel is read before the tool runs on both hosts. The two hosts name the same file differently in the payload: the VS Code extension sends hookName PreToolUse, the CLI/SDK sends its own event name tool_call; both are mapped, and every payload carries clineVersion, which no other vendor sends. Fail-open on both hosts: a hook that times out, crashes or prints something other than JSON is logged and the tool runs. Escalate and transform degrade to a block: hooks cannot ask the user, and the documented contract says a hook cannot modify the tool's parameters. UserPromptSubmit and TaskStart are detect only: the CLI runs them detached, so their cancel is never read there. PostToolUse is detect only: its cancel stops the task after the tool already ran. run_commands' command list arrives as JSON text in preToolUse.parameters and is read as one command per line; apply_patch's target path lives inside the patch text and is not extracted. Install writes .clinerules/hooks/<Event> with a #!/bin/sh shebang and the executable bit, read by both hosts (.cline/hooks/ is read by the CLI/SDK only), and refuses to overwrite a hook file it did not write: Cline runs one file per event name per directory. Hooks must be enabled in the VS Code extension's settings, and run on macOS and Linux only. Tool calls executed inside a provider's own agent loop (Claude Code, Codex as providers) never reach the hook pipeline, per the maintainers on cline/cline#13277. Instruction files reach it through AGENTS.md. Evidence wanted (to test or overturn this row): https://github.com/open-coder-ai/agentseam/issues/178

openhands.notes: PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit and Stop can block; a block at Stop keeps the conversation going. The verdict is the flat {decision: deny, reason} body, and a bare allow is silence (exit 0). No rewrite and no ask: a transform or escalate degrades to a block, never to a silent pass. Fail-open: the docs say any exit code other than 0 and 2 is an error and the operation proceeds. The event name rides under event_type, not hook_event_name, which is what separates OpenHands payloads from every other adapter's. The cwd is working_dir. Known limit: file_editor's own sub-command (view, create, str_replace, insert, undo_edit) arrives in tool_input.command, the same key as terminal's shell command, so Event.command carries it for file_editor calls; a shell policy should check event.tool. The docs document only the project file; a user-level ~/.openhands/hooks.json exists in the SDK source, and a project file shadows it rather than merging. The standalone OpenHands-CLI repository says it is no longer actively maintained; the hooks docs still list the CLI. Instruction files reach it through AGENTS.md (https://docs.openhands.dev/overview/skills). Evidence wanted (to test or overturn this row): https://github.com/open-coder-ai/agentseam/issues/181

kiro.notes: Unadapted, not none: Kiro has a real command-hook surface, but its dialect is one no agentseam family speaks. The config is a versioned list of named hooks with a trigger and an action object, which no install wrapper writes; the verdict is an exit code only, and the IDE and CLI read it differently (IDE: any non-zero exit blocks Pre Tool Use; CLI: only exit 2 blocks, other codes fail open); and the payload is Claude-shaped (hook_event_name, cwd, session_id, tool_name, tool_input) with no key that separates it from a Claude Code payload. Building it means a new family module, which is a core change outside a vendor-config batch. Value-based detection (D1) now declines a Kiro payload naming an MCP tool as mcp_<server>_<tool> (Claude Code spells it mcp__<server>__<tool>) or a tool alias Claude Code never sends (fs_read, fsRead, fs_write, fsWrite, execute_bash, execute_cmd, use_aws; kiro.dev/docs/reference/built-in-tools, updated 2026-10-10), so it detects as no agent. Kiro is not a supported target: do not wire agentseam into it by hand. D2a (2026-10-11) re-checked this and kept the row unadapted: D1's detection covers only part of Kiro's documented events (the alias and mcp_<server>_<tool> tool calls), not the V3 primary-tool or tool-less payloads, and an adapter cannot claim those without making Claude Code payloads ambiguous; the exit-code-only verdict and the versioned hook file would also need a new family. The docs also disagree on the timeout field (timeout in seconds, default 60, vs timeout_ms, default 30,000). Built-in tools are execute_bash (execute_pwsh on Windows) and fs_write, fs_append, str_replace, delete_file. Instruction files reach it through AGENTS.md. factory_droid.notes: Adapted (D2a): Droid's hooks speak the Claude Code dialect, and its payload carries the same keys as a Claude Code payload, including transcript_path and permission_mode, the markers agentseam uses to recognise Claude Code. A value separates them: every Droid payload carries permission_mode with one of Droid's own values (off, spec, auto-low, auto-medium, auto-high), which Claude Code never sends, so claude_code declines such a payload and factory_droid claims it (claims.accept_values). If a Droid build ever sent a Claude Code permission_mode value, the payload would read as claude_code again, whose deny Droid also honours. A deny is hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: deny at PreToolUse and decision: block at UserPromptSubmit and Stop. Escalate and transform degrade to a block: Droid's documented ask does not force a prompt in 0.238.0 (it falls through to the autonomy level's normal permission flow, which may auto-approve), and updatedInput is merged into the original input rather than replacing it, so a transform cannot remove a field. Shell policies see Execute; write policies see Create, Edit, MultiEdit and ApplyPatch, whose patch text is read as content but whose target path lives inside the patch and is not extracted. Install writes .factory/hooks.json keyed directly by event name, the documented project file; Droid snapshots hooks at startup, so a new hook applies to the next session. Fail mode is documented only for non-2 exits (fail-open); timeout and malformed-output behaviour are not documented. The Notification event is not mapped. Instruction files reach it through AGENTS.md. Evidence wanted (to test or overturn this row): https://github.com/open-coder-ai/agentseam/issues/184
